about: Relay satellites that may carry a lander's data to Earth, with their launch status, and real lunar orbiters used only to check the pass calculation. A relay's contribution is worked out only from a published or entered orbit, and is shown as a range 'if it flies as planned'. Queqiao-2 is not listed: it publishes no orbit a CLPS mission could book.

Blue Ghost Mission 2 Gets Stacked at JPL (PIA26598, 16 December 2025)

inclination_deg.reason: Two inclinations are given for it: 46.8 deg (ESA's slides) and 54.9 deg (SSTL's Small Satellite Conference paper), neither with its reference plane. Both ends are swept; the value is their middle.

arg_periapsis_deg.reason: Not published. ESA and SSTL describe an orbit favouring the south pole, which puts the far point over the south pole: an argument of periapsis near 90 deg (NASA's reference frozen orbits for the south pole keep it between 85.4 and 92.5 deg). Swept from 85 to 95 deg.

period_h.reason: Worked out from the perilune and apolune heights by Kepler's third law (the Moon's GM from DE440); not stated as a figure to check against.

notes: The perilune and apolune heights (673.4 and 7331.8 km) and the two inclinations were read from the search index of ESA's slides and SSTL's paper: both files sit behind a bot check from this network, so they are to be checked against the documents themselves.
records.name: Lunar Pathfinder
records.operator: ESA, built and operated by Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd
records.launch_note: To fly on Firefly's Blue Ghost Mission 2, integrated into its Elytra Dark orbital vehicle. ESA: launch not earlier than November 2026; SSTL: due to launch 2027.
records.orbit_note: SSTL: 'a stable elliptical orbit to provide long duration visibility of the Southern Lunar Hemisphere each day' (an elliptical lunar frozen orbit). Its heights are ESA's; where its node and its place along the orbit will be is not published, so both are swept.

periapsis_km.reason: Altus-1's orbit is not published (NASA: deployed 'in lunar orbit'). Assumed to be one of the five elliptical frozen orbits of NASA's reference design for the lunar relay constellation (LCRNS 3.1, Table 1, Moon principal-axis frame), whose final design belongs to Intuitive Machines under its Near Space Network contract; the range covers all five.

records.name: Altus-1 data-relay satellite
records.launch_note: Planned to fly alongside IM-3 (NASA, August 2026).
records.orbit_note: NASA says only that Altus-1 is deployed 'in lunar orbit'. The orbit used here is assumed from NASA's reference design; where its node and its place along the orbit will be is swept.

notes: Used only to check the pass calculation against a real orbit. Not a relay for any CLPS lander, and never shown as one.
